parts.text:
Find the first 4 terms, in ascending powers of $x$, of the binomial expansion of
$\left(3-\frac{1}{3}x\right)^5$
giving each term in its simplest form.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\left(3-\frac{1}{3}x\right)^5$: $3^5+{}^5C_1 3^4\left(-\frac{1}{3}x\right)+{}^5C_2 3^3\left(-\frac{1}{3}x\right)^2+{}^5C_3 3^2\left(-\frac{1}{3}x\right)^3\ldots$
First term of 243 B1
$({}^5C_1\times\ldots\times x)+({}^5C_2\times\ldots\times x^2)+({}^5C_3\times\ldots\times x^3)\ldots$ M1
$=(243\ldots)-\frac{405}{3}x+\frac{270}{9}x^2-\frac{90}{27}x^3\ldots$ A1
$=(243\ldots)-135x+30x^2-\frac{10}{3}x^3\ldots$ A1
Alternative method: $\left(3-\frac{1}{3}x\right)^5=3^5\left(1-\frac{x}{9}\right)^5=3^5\left(1+{}^5C_1\left(-\frac{1}{9}x\right)+{}^5C_2\left(-\frac{1}{9}x\right)^2+{}^5C_3\left(-\frac{1}{9}x\right)^3\ldots\right)$, scheme applied exactly as before.
Notes: B1: constant term 243 in expansion. M1: two of the three binomial coefficients correct and with correct power of $x$; accept $^5C_1$ or $\binom{5}{1}$ or 5, $^5C_2$ or $\binom{5}{2}$ or 10, $^5C_3$ or $\binom{5}{3}$ or 10; Pascal's triangle may be used; if only first two terms included M1 may still be awarded. A1: two of the final three terms correct (may be unsimplified). A1: all three final terms correct and simplified (accept $-3\frac{1}{3}$ or $-3.\dot{3}$ for $-\frac{10}{3}$; not $3.3$). Common error $3^5+{}^5C_1 3^4(-\frac{1}{3})x+{}^5C_2 3^3(-\frac{1}{3})x^2+{}^5C_3 3^2(-\frac{1}{3})x^3=(243)-135x-90x^2-30x^3$ earns B1,M1,A0,A0. If extra terms given then isw. No negative signs in answer also earns B1,M1,A0,A0. If series divided through by 3 at final stage after an error resulting in all multiples of three coefficients, apply scheme to series before this division and ignore subsequent work (isw). Special Case: only gives first three terms $=(243\ldots)-135x+30x^2\ldots$ or $243-\frac{405}{3}x+\frac{270}{9}x^2$: follow scheme to give B1 M1 A1 A0 special case (do not treat as misread). Answers such as $243+405-\frac{1}{3}x+270-\frac{1}{9}x^2+90-\frac{1}{27}x^3\ldots$ gain no credit as binomial coefficients are not linked to the $x$ terms.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- A1: Two of the final three terms correct – may be unsimplified i.e. two of $-135x+30x^2-\frac{10}{3}x^3$ correct, or two of $-\frac{405}{3}x+\frac{270}{9}x^2-\frac{90}{27}x^3$ (may be just two terms)
- A1: All three final terms correct and simplified. (Can be listed with commas or appear on separate lines. Accept in reverse order.) Accept correct alternatives to $-\frac{10}{3}$ e.g. $-3\frac{1}{3}$ or $-3.\dot{3}$ the recurring must be clear. 3.3 is not acceptable. Allow e.g. $+-135x$

parts.text:
In the triangle $ABC$, $AB=16$ cm, $AC=13$ cm, angle $ABC=50^\circ$ and angle $BCA=x^\circ$
Find the two possible values for $x$, giving your answers to one decimal place.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\frac{\sin x}{16}=\frac{\sin 50^\circ}{13}$ M1
$(\sin x=)\frac{16\times\sin 50}{13}$ ($=0.943$ but accept 0.94) A1
$x=$ awrt $70.5(3)$ and $109.5$ or $70.6$ and $109.4$ dM1 A1
Notes: M1: use sine formula correctly in any form; allow awrt 0.77 for $\sin 50^\circ$. A1: give the correct value or correct expression for $\sin x$ (implies M1 mark); if given as expression they do not need degrees symbol, $\frac{\sin 50\times16}{13}$ is fine; if given as decimal allow answers which round to 0.94; allow awrt $-0.323$ (radians) here but no further marks available; if they give this as $x$ (not $\sin x$) and do not recover this is A0. dM1: correct work leading to $x=\ldots$ (via inverse sin) expression or value for $\sin x$; if previous A mark awarded for correct expression then for getting to awrt 70.5 or 109.5 (allow for 70.6 or 109.4); if previous A mark not gained but rounding errors made in rearranging correct sine formula then award dM1 for evidence of use of inverse sin in degrees on their value for $\sin x$; NB 70.5 following a correct sine formula will gain M1A1M1. A1: deduce and state both answers $x=70.5$ and $109.5$ (do not need degrees), accept awrt these; also accept 70.6 and 109.4 (second answer sometimes obtained by long indirect route but still scores A1). If working in radians throughout, answers are 1.23 and 1.91, awarded M1A1M1A0 (working with 50 radians gives probable answers of $-0.3288$ and $3.47$ giving M1A1M1A0). Special case: wrong labelling of triangle simplifies problem so only one solution for angle $x$; not treated as misread; if missing side found as awrt 12.6 then proceed to find an angle or its cosine or sine then give M1A0M0A0. Alternative Method using cosine rule: let $BC=a$. M1: uses cosine rule to form three term quadratic equation in $a$ (e.g. $a^2-32a\cos50^\circ+87=0$ or $a^2-\text{awrt }20.6a+87=0$, allow slips in signs rearranging). A1: solves and obtains correct value for $a$ of awrt 14.6 or awrt 5.95. dM1: correct full method to find at least one of the two angles (may use cosine rule again, or find angle $BAC$ then use sine rule); as in main scheme, if previous A mark awarded then should obtain one correct angle for this mark. A1: deduces both correct answers as in main scheme. NB obtaining only one correct angle will usually score M1A1M1A0 in any method.

$\int_0^2\left(5^x+\log_2(x+1)\right)dx$

questions.stem:
Figure 1 is a sketch representing the cross-section of a large tent $ABCDEF$.
$AB$ and $DE$ are line segments of equal length.
Angle $FAB$ and angle $DEF$ are equal.
$F$ is the midpoint of the straight line $AE$ and $FC$ is perpendicular to $AE$.
$BCD$ is an arc of a circle of radius 3.5 m with centre at $F$.
It is given that
$AF=FE=3.7\text{ m}$
$BF=FD=3.5\text{ m}$
angle $BFD=1.77$ radians
Find

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) the length of the arc $BCD$ in metres to 2 decimal places,
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
Usually answered in radians: uses $BCD=3.5\times(\text{angle})=3.5\times1.77=6.195$ (m) (accept awrt 6.20) M1 A1
Notes: M1: uses $s=3.5\times\theta$ with $\theta$ in radians or completely correct work in degrees. A1: awrt 6.20 or just 6.2 (do not need units); correct answer can imply the method.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) the area of the sector $FBCD$ in m$^2$ to 2 decimal places,
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
Area $=\frac{1}{2}(3.5)^2\times1.77=10.84$ (m$^2$) M1 A1
Notes: M1: for attempt to use $A=\frac{1}{2}\times3.5^2\times\theta$ (accept $\theta$ in degrees). A1: for awrt 10.84 (do not need units) isw if correct answer followed by 10.8; correct answer can imply the method.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) the total area of the cross-section of the tent in m$^2$ to 2 decimal places.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
Area of triangle $=\frac{1}{2}\times3.7\times3.5\times\sin(\text{angle})=\frac{1}{2}\times3.7\times3.5\times\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{1.77}{2}\right)$ ($=$awrt 4.1) M1, A1
Total area $=$"10.84"$+2\times$"4.101"$=19.04$ M1, A1cao
Notes: M1: uses area of triangle $\frac{1}{2}\times3.7\times3.5\times\sin(\text{angle})$; must be correct method for area of triangle but may be less direct. A1: correct expression using correct angle i.e. $\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{1.77}{2}$ or awrt 0.69 or awrt 39 degrees (need at least 2sf if no other work seen, but may be implied by correct final answer); if correct expression given then isw (so e.g. isw an answer of 0.0775 implying angle set to degrees on calculator). M1: adds twice their second calculated area (even if rectangle or segment) to their sector area (may have been slips or errors in one or both formulae such as missing $\frac{1}{2}$ or mixture of degrees and radians or weak attempt at triangle area) so M0A0M1A0 is a possible mark distribution. A1: 19.04 cao (common answer through insufficient accuracy is 19.08 which loses final mark). Special Case: mark profile M1A0M1A0M1A0M1A0 can be given if the angle is misunderstood as $1.77\pi$ or as $AFB$ for example. If "10.84"$+3.5\times3.7\sin(\text{angle})$ used this can gain both M marks and A marks if correct; but use of $3.5\times3.7\sin(\text{angle})$ later doubled and added to "10.84" is 1st M0, 2nd M1.

questions.stem:
Figure 2 shows a sketch of part of the curve with equation
$y=4x^3+9x^2-30x-8,\quad -0.5\leqslant x\leqslant2.2$
The curve has a turning point at the point $A$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Using calculus, show that the $x$ coordinate of $A$ is 1
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
$\frac{dy}{dx}=12x^2+18x-30$ M1
Either substitute $x=1$ to give $\frac{dy}{dx}=12+18-30=0$ A1, so turning point (all correct work so far) A1cso
Or solve $\frac{dy}{dx}=12x^2+18x-30=0$ to give $x=\ldots$ A1, deduce $x=1$ from correct work A1cso
Notes: M1: attempt at differentiation - all powers reduced by 1 with $8\to0$. A1: the derivative must be correct and uses derivative $=0$ to find $x$ or substitutes $x=1$ to give 0; ignore any reference to the other root $(-5/2)$ for this mark. A1cso: obtains $x=1$ from correct work, or deduces turning point (if substitution used, may be implied by a preamble e.g. dy/dx$=0$ at T.P.). N.B. If their factorisation or their second root is incorrect then award A0cso. If however their factorisation/roots are correct, it is not necessary for them to comment that $-2.5$ is outside the range given.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The curve crosses the $x$-axis at the points $B(2,0)$ and $C\left(-\frac{1}{4},0\right)$
The finite region $R$, shown shaded in Figure 2, is bounded by the curve, the line $AB$, and the $x$-axis.
(b) Use integration to find the area of the finite region $R$, giving your answer to 2 decimal places.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
Way 1: When $x=1$, $y=4+9-30-8=-25$ B1

$=(-19)-\frac{261}{256}$ or $-19-1.02$
So Area $=$"their 12.5"+"their $20\frac{5}{256}$" or "12.5"+"20.02" or "12.5"+"their $\frac{5125}{256}$" ddM1
$=32.52$ (NOT $-32.52$) A1

Notes (a): as above. Notes (b) Way 1: B1 obtains $y=-25$ when $x=1$ (may be seen anywhere, even in (a)) or finds correct equation of line is $y=25x-50$. B1: obtains area of triangle $=12.5$ (may be seen anywhere), allow $-12.5$, accept $\frac12\times1\times25$. M1: attempt at integration of cubic; two correct terms for their integration; no limits needed. A1: completely correct integral for the cubic (may be unsimplified). dM1: (dependent on previous M) for start of correct method (dependent on previous M) — substituting 1 and $-1/4$ and subtracting; may use 2 and $-1/4$ and also 2 and 1 AND subtract (equivalent). ddM1: (depends on both method marks) correct method to obtain shaded area so adds two positive numbers (areas) together — one is area of triangle, the other is area of region obtained from integration of correct function with correct limits (may add two negatives then make positive). Then mark as before if they use Method in original scheme
- Way 2: This is a long method and needs to be a correct method. B1: Finds $y=-25$ at $x=1$, or correct equation of line is $y=25x-50$. B1: May be implied where WAY 2 is used and final correct answer obtained so award of final A1 results in the award of this B1. It may also be implied by correct integration of line equation or of curve minus line expression between limits 1 and 2. So if only slip is final subtraction (giving final A0, this mark may still be awarded) So may be implied by 4.5 seen for area of "segment shaped" region between line and curve.
- M1: Attempt at integration of given cubic or after attempt at subtracting their line equation (no limits needed). Two correct terms needed.
